claims: The Terraform test will fail: `alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69` — test still requires `peg_slack_title` to contain `$alert.Annotations.summary` and `$alert.Annotations.resolved_summary`, but the new title at `peg-message-templates.tf:14` contains neither; only the JS lint test was updated

Error → Alerting is a regression (`peg-alert-events.ts:106-109, 318-321`): now `error-recovered-alerting` only closes the error cycle, so when the alert later clears the clear has no matching fired row and loses its "lasted N" duration
Error → Alerting: the active row reads "Grafana can evaluate … again; its alert condition is active" instead of the breach cause

Alerting → Error → Normal is left open: the alert cycle opened at the first Alerting never closes, so the list shows "Monitoring recovered" next to an "Urgent alert active" row for an alert Grafana already resolved
The two new tests start from Normal → Error and Alerting → Error → Alerting, so neither broken sequence is tested

Three fail-closed tests now pass no matter what: `route.test.ts:819, 832, 846` — `.mockResolvedValue(json(stateFrame([])))` hands the same `Response` object to fetch calls 2, 3 and 4; the locked stream throws and returns 502, so the malformed-frame, oversized-body and row-limit tests pass even if the guard is deleted; the row-limit guard is effectively untested

Wrong copy for rules with no source: `peg-alert-events.ts:230` — `pegAlertSourceName("")` returns "Price source", so a Grafana error on the seven rules with `source = ""` reads "Grafana could not evaluate the Price source Peg rule"
Grafana history requests double, undoing a fix from last week: `route.ts:43-83` — `fetchJson` quietly makes two requests, so each refresh sends 4 requests instead of 2, reverting #1875's reduction
`route.ts:43-83`: worst-case body memory goes from 8 MB to 16 MB
`route.ts:43-83`: the fan-out is hidden inside `fetchJson` rather than being clear in `GET`
Slack previews may show only an emoji: `peg-message-templates.tf:14` — Grafana's Slack notifier uses the title as fallback text, so notification previews show just "🚨" or "✅" with no cause
Stale docs: `docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md` lines 118-119 still say Slack titles contain the icon plus the summary
Stale docs: `docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md` lines 131-132 still say the history backend "reads only fired and resolved transitions" but it now also reads Error transitions

judge_reasoning.3830366234: Review finding 1 says peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69 still requires summary/resolved_summary in the title, which the new icon-only title lacks, so terraform test fails.
judge_reasoning.3830366243: Review finding 7 says docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md lines 118-119 still claim Slack titles contain the icon plus the summary.
judge_reasoning.3830366247: The review never discusses Error → Pending recoveries or the missing Pending query in errorStateHistoryUrl. It only mentions #1875 cutting Pending requests, in a request-count context.
judge_reasoning.3830366547: Review finding 2 says that after Alerting → Error → Normal the alert cycle never closes, so an active alert row shows next to 'Monitoring recovered'.
judge_reasoning.3830366556: The review does not identify error cycles orphaned by Error → Pending → Alerting transitions.
judge_reasoning.3830371307: The review does not flag fragile slicing or unscoped link checks in the lint test. It explicitly says the lint test's slice is correct.
judge_reasoning.3830371315: Review finding 3 says the shared Response from mockResolvedValue makes getReader throw on reuse, so the fail-closed tests return 502 regardless of the guard.
judge_reasoning.3830371325: Review finding 2 covers error-recovered-alerting only closing the error cycle and not opening or pairing the alert cycle at peg-alert-events.ts pairing logic. This is the same error-recovery pairing defect at line 352.
judge_reasoning.3830416461: Review finding 4 says pegAlertSourceName("") returns 'Price source' for source-less rules (Structural Saturation, Indexed Pool, Heartbeat, Policy Rollover) at peg-alert-events.ts:230.

1.why: peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69 still asserts the title template contains $alert.Annotations.summary and resolved_summary, which the new title dropped. This is the known 'Update the stale Terraform title assertion' item.

2.why: transitionKind now maps Error→Alerting to error-recovered-alerting, and cycleKey sends it to the ':error' key, so no alert cycle opens. A later Alerting→Normal clear finds nothing open under the ':alert' key, goes to unpairedCleared, and gets no 'lasted' duration. Before this change, Error→Alerting counted as 'raised'.

3.why: evaluationCause does give this lead for recovered-alerting, but that is deliberate: the new test 'keeps Alerting to Error to Alerting separate from breach copy' asserts it. This is a copy preference, not a concrete defect.

4.why: Alerting opens the ':alert' cycle, then Error→Normal (error-recovered) closes only the ':error' cycle, so the alert cycle stays open and is emitted as active. This is the known 'Error recovery leaves breach active' item (peg-alert-events.ts:352).

5.why: True that the two new route.test.ts cases cover only Normal→Error→Normal and Alerting→Error→Alerting. But this is a test-coverage remark that restates claims 2 and 4, not a separate defect.

6.why: route.test.ts:819/832/846 changed to mockResolvedValue with a single json(...) Response that gets reused. This is the known route.test.ts:819 item.

7.why: pegAlertSourceName returns 'Price source' when the provider is empty, and evaluationCause uses it in the lead. This is the known peg-alert-events.ts:230 'Label source-less evaluation failures by rule' item.

8.why: fetchJson does now fetch twice per URL (4 requests total; the test expects 4). But Error transitions need separate state-history filters, so the extra requests are intentional and no concrete failure is shown. Also, #1875 is from 2026-08-17, not last week.

9.why: True in arithmetic: four bodies at PEG_ALERTS_MAX_STATE_RESPONSE_BYTES (4 MB each) is 16 MB. But it is a resource tradeoff with no concrete defect.

10.why: Only a style preference about where the fan-out lives (errorStateHistoryUrl inside fetchJson vs in GET). It names no bug.

11.why: The new peg.slack.title renders only the icon (🚨/🟡/✅). Grafana's Slack notifier uses the rendered title as the attachment fallback text, so push previews lose the cause the old title carried.

12.why: docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md (doc_type: runbook) line 118-119 still says 'Slack titles use the severity icon plus that summary'. This is the known 'Keep the Peg runbook aligned with the new title' item.

13.why: docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:132 still says 'reads only fired and resolved transitions', but route.ts errorStateHistoryUrl now also queries current=Error and previous=Error. The known runbook item covers only the title.
